cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Access Has a Price
cards.instruction: Turn every piece of access, information, or approval into a favor, debt, or condition.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I'll introduce you to the curator if you hang my exhibition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hang it Saturday. Can you send her portfolio requirements now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Of course. Could you collect my frames too?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. Give me her email; I'll ask her directly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Direct access includes taking the show down. Shall I put you down for Sunday?

mechanism: A grants only priced forms of curator access, assigning progressively more exhibition labor as the condition of each permission.
confusable: D42 exchanging favors could complete one bargain; D70 makes each additional information request incur another condition.
comparison: Art-world contact access differs from a physically locked mop cupboard.
seedUse: Use D70-b Saturday hanging, frame pickup and Sunday removal while replacing polite equal bargaining with explicit grant of terms.
